mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 650K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer discretionary spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 650K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) drops below 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by > 200K in a month, a tightening labor market drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as firms increase investments.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% YoY signals increased economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as firms ramp up production to meet demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 45% of instances when INDPRO growth > 2% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 1.2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP (GDPC1) growth above 3% QoQ indicates strong aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as consumer and business spending boost economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 35% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3% QoQ, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher borrowing costs reduce consumption and investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1.2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 10% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) contracts by > 100K in a month, a weakening labor market drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as firms reduce investments.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 30% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) growth below -2% MoM indicates declining consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as reduced demand hurts firms' revenues.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS growth < -2% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 0.8-year rolling window.
